@graph.name: 2026 Florida Managed Areas
@graph.description:
The Florida Natural Areas Inventory is the primary source for information on Florida's conservation lands. FNAI's database includes boundaries and statistics for more than 2,900 federal, state, local, and private managed areas, all provided directly by the managing agencies. National parks, state forests, wildlife management areas, local and private preserves are examples of the managed areas included. The shapefile is called FLMA for Florida Managed Areas; updated versions are published quarterly.
  
  FLORIDA CONSERVATION LANDS (layer name FLMA): This is a polygon data layer for public (and some private) lands that the Florida Natural Areas Inventory (FNAI) has identified as having natural resource value and that are being managed at least partially for conservation purposes. The term "Managed Area" refers to a managed conservation land.

additionalProperty.name: process_step
additionalProperty.value:
#########
  # GDSC ETL is performed in two steps: shell script to ETL data into postgres
  # and then additional transformations with SQL in postGIS (if needed).
  ####
  
  #########
  # Step 1 - bash script (pseudo code)
  ####
  
  # create directory structure and move into it
  mkdir -p /data/fl_2026_flma/download -p /data/fl_2026_flma/etl
  chmod -R 777 /data/fl_2026_flma
  cd /data/fl_2026_flma
  
  # set update flag based on last update and update frequency
  do_update=0 if date() < last_update + update_frequency else do_update = 1
  
  # download if update flag is set:
  if do_update == 1 then
  wget --retry-connrefused --waitretry=1 --read-timeout=20 --timeout=15 -t 10 -O download/fl_2026_flma.zip 'https://www.fnai.org/shapefiles/flma_202603.zip' 2>&1
  
  # unzip to download directory if update flag is set
  if do_update == 1 then
  unzip -o download/fl_2026_flma.zip -d download && rm download/fl_2026_flma.zip 2>&1
  
  # load into postGIS with:
  ogr2ogr -lco GEOMETRY_NAME=geom -f PostgreSQL PG:"<postgres connection>" download/FloridaConservationLands.gdb -lco PRECISION=NO -nlt multipolygon -nln fl_2026_flma
  echo success: FloridaConservationLands.gdb loaded with ogr2ogr
  
  
  #########
  # Step 2 - SQL script (pseudo code):
  ####
  
  # remove duplicate points and make geometries valid:
  UPDATE fl_2026_flma
    SET geom=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(geom));
  
  # add local geometry column and reproject existing geometries into local EPSG:
  ALTER TABLE fl_2026_flma DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS geom_local CASCADE;
  SELECT AddGeometryColumn (
    'fl_2026_flma',
    'geom_local', 2236, 'multipolygon', 2
  );
  UPDATE fl_2026_flma
    SET geom_local=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(ST_Transform(ST_Multi(geom),2236)));
  CREATE INDEX fl_2026_flma_geom_local_idx
    ON fl_2026_flma
    USING GIST (geom_local);
  NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';
